headline: Funding flows. Strategies shift. Bureaucracy hums.
deck: This week, space startups secure significant funding while government priorities evolve.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly has successfully raised $190 million in a Series C funding round, pushing its valuation to $1.6 billion. The investment underscores the growing demand for co-orbital security solutions, particularly from defense sectors. With the Department of Defense's increasing focus on space domain awareness, True Anomaly is well-positioned to capitalize on this trend.
stories.soWhat: In a world where cash flow trumps tech, True Anomaly's funding suggests that investors are betting on the necessity of security over flashy innovations.

stories.head: Contrivian challenges multi-orbit satellite strategies
stories.body: Startup Contrivian is making waves by arguing that LEO satellites may outperform multi-orbit setups by simplifying networking challenges. This approach could disrupt established players who have invested heavily in complex multi-orbit architectures, potentially reshaping market dynamics. As satellite networks become increasingly congested, Contrivian's strategy could resonate with customers looking for straightforward solutions.
stories.soWhat: If simplicity wins in space, expect a shake-up among those who thought complexity was the key to success.

stories.head: Portal Space partners with Quindar for military missions
stories.body: Portal Space has contracted Quindar for ground mission support as it prepares to launch maneuverable spacecraft designed for military applications. This partnership highlights the increasing demand for flexibility in military space operations, especially as geopolitical tensions rise. The financial terms of the deal remain undisclosed, but the implications for future military contracts could be significant.
stories.soWhat: With more military players seeking maneuverability, the procurement landscape is likely to favor those who can adapt quickly—good luck to the slow movers.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on the FCC's next moves
watchlist.body: With Lynk and Anterix's recent FCC approval, expect more regulatory developments that could impact satellite communications.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser launch timeline
watchlist.body: After passing its critical design review, the timeline for the Dream Chaser's launch could provide insights into future military transport capabilities.

watchlist.title: Budget discussions for FY27 heat up
watchlist.body: The additional $1.4 billion for space resilience in the FY27 budget could lead to increased competition for government contracts.

watchlist.title: SpaceX secondary market valuation implications
watchlist.body: SpaceX's secondary market valuation of $470 billion might influence investor sentiment across the space sector, especially for upcoming IPOs.

talent.statLabel: Week-over-week growth in resumes from primes to Series B/C
talent.head: Talent is leaving big-aero — and it's not about money
talent.body: Compensation is not the gating factor. The complaint, almost universally, is schedule risk — the inability to ship anything quickly, the half-decade gap between joining and seeing flight hardware, the meeting that exists to schedule the meeting. The startups absorbing this talent will, in two years, be hard to compete with on a level playing field.
